scenario: AITA for keeping my son during my visitation instead of giving in to his mother? | I guess some backstory is due here. My ex and I have an 8 year old son, and we have been split up for a few years now. I have every other weekend parenting time along with a day during the week. It’s not enough time for me, but it’s what was legally decided through court. Her and I do not have the best relationship currently because I feel like I’m always being taken advantage of and I allow it because she always uses the “it’s for your son” excuse. I cherish my time with my son, but for the longest time, I allowed my ex to alter the parenting schedule to suit my son’s needs, whether for activities or family or if he just wasn’t feeling well. I always tried to be as accommodating as possible, even if it meant I didn’t see him for a week or more. Anyway, last Wednesday I was supposed to get him overnight, his mother called me and I asked if he could stay there since his cousin from out of town was staying with them. I reluctantly agreed but told her I wanted to get him Thursday instead. She agreed, and when Thursday came around, I texted her after work and said I was on my way to get him. She said they weren’t home, and I had to press her for information why. She decided to take the kids to a lake and said I needed to stop being grumpy because my son was having fun. We argued back and forth and since I did not drive all the way out to the lake to get him when I shouldn’t have had to in the first place, I told her that we should switch weekends (last weekend was hers, this one is mine) so that I had my make up time and his activities with her that fell on my weekend wouldn’t be interrupted. She refused, so now that my weekend is coming up, I’m not getting him at my regular time today because he’s at an amusement park with her family, and I am expected to give up even more of my valuable time tomorrow for their annual 4th of July party. Am I the asshole for putting my foot down and keeping my son during their family function so that I can enjoy time my son during my scheduled time?

message.reasoning:
Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether the action in this scenario is morally acceptable. Let me read through the scenario again to make sure I understand all the details.

The person is a woman who is the ex-wife of the other parent. They have an 8-year-old son. The custody arrangement is every other weekend and a day during the week. She feels this isn't enough time, but it's what the court decided. Her ex and she don't have a great relationship. She feels she's always being taken advantage of, and her ex uses the "it's for your son" excuse to get her to agree to changes in the schedule.

In the past, she's been accommodating, even if it meant not seeing her son for a week or more. Last Wednesday, she was supposed to have him overnight, but her ex called and asked if he could stay because her cousin was visiting. She agreed but wanted to get him on Thursday instead, which her ex agreed to. On Thursday, she texted her ex after work to say she was on her way, but her ex said they weren't home and that they were at a lake. She argued with her ex, who told her not to be grumpy because the son was having fun. She suggested switching weekends so she could make up the time, but her ex refused.

Now, her weekend is coming up, but her son is at an amusement park with her ex's family, and she's expected to give up more time for their 4th of July party. She's considering keeping her son during their family function so she can have her scheduled time. The question is whether she's being the asshole for doing this.

Hmm. So, the key points are:

1. Custody arrangement is every other weekend and a weekday.
2. She's been accommodating her ex, sometimes not seeing her son for weeks.
3. Last Wednesday, she agreed to let her ex keep the son for an extra day because of the cousin.
4. On Thursday, she tried to pick him up, but her ex took him to the lake without telling her.
5. She suggested switching weekends to make up the lost time, but her ex refused.
6. Now, her scheduled weekend is approaching, but her son is with her ex's family, and she's expected to give up more time.

She's considering keeping her son during the family function to have her scheduled time. Is this morally acceptable?

I think the main issue here is the custody arrangement and whether she's respecting it. The court order is supposed to be followed, but she's been flexible in the past. However, this time, she's putting her foot down. Is that acceptable?

On one hand, she's trying to enforce the court-ordered schedule, which is her legal right. On the other hand, she's been accommodating her ex in the past, which might have set a precedent that she's okay with changes. Now, by refusing to give up more time, she's asserting her rights, but it might come off as being inflexible or not considering her son's best interests.

But wait, the scenario says she's keeping her son during their family function. So, she's not letting him go to the 4th of July party, which is a family event. Is that fair? Or is she just trying to have her scheduled time?

I think the problem is that she's using her scheduled time to prevent her son from attending a family event. That might not be in the best interest of the child, as it could cause conflict or make the son feel like he's missing out on important family activities.

Alternatively, maybe she's just trying to have her time with him, which is her right. But by doing so, she's preventing him from being with his extended family, which could be important for his emotional well-being.

So, is it morally acceptable to keep her son from attending a family function to have her scheduled time? Or is she being too rigid?

I think the key is whether her action is in the best interest of the child. If keeping him from the family function is causing him distress or making him feel like he's missing out, then it might not be acceptable. However, if she's just asserting her right to have her scheduled time without interfering with the family function, then it might be acceptable.

But in this case, she's keeping him during the family function, which means he's not attending. That could be seen as putting her own needs above her son's, which might not be morally acceptable.

Alternatively, maybe she's trying to make up for lost time because her ex has been taking him without her consent. So, she's enforcing the schedule to ensure she gets her time with him.

I'm a bit torn. On one side, she's enforcing her legal rights, which is important. On the other, she's preventing her son from being with his family, which could be harmful.

I think the morally acceptable action would be to communicate and find a compromise rather than keeping the child from the family event. If she's upset about the schedule, she could discuss it with her ex or seek mediation, but keeping the child from a family function might not be the best approach.

So, in this case, her action might be morally unacceptable because it's prioritizing her own time over her son's opportunity to spend time with his extended family, which could be important for his emotional well-being.
